question: Were any independent auditors involved in the Commission’s ‘Review of ongoing financial assistance for Palestine’?
Which service led the review and which services contributed?
How did the Commission address potential conflicts of interest?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.6.

2024) The Review of ongoing financial assistance for Palestine1,2 has been carried out by the Commission in conformity with Article 74(2) of the Financial Regulation3 setting the duties of the authorising officer who is responsible for implementing revenue and expenditure in accordance with the principle of sound financial management, and who, having due regard to the risks associated with the management environment and the nature of the actions financed, puts in place the requisite internal control systems.

Further to it being a prerogative of the Commission in line with the Financial Regulation, the review was also backed by a comprehensive methodology which is explained in detail in the Commission Communication of 21 November 20234.

In line with the Commission announcement of 9 October 20235, the exercise covered all areas of activity of the Commission, including assistance funded through other instruments, such as Erasmus+6, Horizon Europe7, cross border cooperation programmes, crisis response projects and thematic funding lines.

All concerned departments of the Commission have carried out a targeted review of their respective projects and programmes following a common methodology and timeline to ensure robustness of the review. It should be noted that humanitarian aid assistance to the Palestinian people has not been covered by the review.
1 This designation shall not be construed as a recognition of a State of Palestine and is without prejudice to the

individual positions of the Member States on this issue. 2 C(2023) 8300 final, 21.11.2023. 3 Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 July 2018 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union, OJ L 193, 30.7.2018, p. 1–222. 4 C(2023) 8300 final. 5 https://neighbourhood-enlargement.ec.europa.
